identification.summary: Check Point describes EvilWeb as a pro-Russian hacktivist group created in March 2024 that targeted American and European entities in support of the Russian narrative, using a hack-and-leak method in parallel with traditional DDoS attacks [S1]. It claimed to have obtained data from various high-profile American organizations [S1]. Its Telegram channel had 1,146 members as of 2024-09-03 [S1].
identification.notes: Do not confuse with Evil Corp (Indrik Spider), a separate financially motivated Russian cybercrime group; the name similarity is coincidental in the sources reviewed. A Russian-language wiki entry (cyclowiki) names a leader 'Levis'; this was not corroborated and is not used. Malpedia lists the group under a Russia country tag [S5].

attribution.basis: Check Point characterizes the group only as 'pro-Russian' [S1]; Malpedia tags it Russia [S5]. No reviewed source ties it to a Russian government organization, and none is asserted here.

objectives: Check Point states the group acted in support of the Russian narrative [S1]. During #FreeDurov it joined a campaign demanding release of Telegram founder Pavel Durov after his arrest in France [S1][S2].

targeting.notes: Check Point says EvilWeb targeted various American and European entities and claimed data from high-profile American organizations [S1]. The #FreeDurov campaign as a whole targeted more than 50 French targets, primarily with DDoS [S1]; specific sectors hit by EvilWeb itself could not be confirmed from accessible text.

capabilities.summary: The group operates a hack-and-leak model alongside conventional DDoS attacks [S1]. It publicizes claims via a Telegram channel [S1]. Strobes notes no exploited CVEs attributed to it (secondary, undated; not cited as fact). Claimed data thefts were not independently verified in the sources reviewed.

campaigns.name: Group creation
campaigns.summary: EvilWeb was created in March 2024 and began targeting American and European entities using hack-and-leak and DDoS [S1].

campaigns.name: #FreeDurov / #OpDurov participation
campaigns.summary: After Pavel Durov's arrest in France on 2024-08-24, hacktivist groups launched #FreeDurov; EvilWeb announced participation on 2024-08-25 and began DDoS and hacking attacks [S1]. Dozens of groups collaborated against more than 50 French targets, mainly via DDoS [S1]. SC Media reported the observed attacks appeared limited to DDoS disruption rather than exfiltration or ransomware [S3]; Cyber Daily reported disruption appeared largely minimal [S2].

diamond.adversary: Pro-Russian hacktivist collective; no state sponsor identified in reviewed sources [S1][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram channel for announcements and claims [S1]; technical infrastructure not documented in reviewed sources.
diamond.victim: American and European entities; French targets during #FreeDurov [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Support of Russian narrative; opportunistic joining of the #FreeDurov campaign [S1].
diamond.technology: DDoS tooling and data-theft methods not specified in reviewed sources.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Environment: EvilWeb is a low-sophistication, publicity-driven hacktivist actor aligned with Russian narratives that targets US and European entities [S1]. MLCOA: opportunistic DDoS and claimed hack-and-leak against Western public-facing sites when geopolitical triggers arise, as with #FreeDurov, which saw 50+ French targets hit mainly by DDoS [S1], with limited disruption [S2][S3]. MDCOA: leak of genuine data from a US organization amplified by pro-Russian channels [S1]. Candidate indicators: Telegram announcements joining named operations (#Free... hashtags), target lists, and claimed leak posts [S1]. Evidence is thin; reassess if new reporting emerges.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: monitor open-source Telegram claims by hacktivist groups, noting claims can be exaggerated and impact is often minimal [S2][S3]. Authorities: monitoring public channels is open-source collection; any defensive response to DDoS on civilian sites follows owner/operator and national cyber authorities. Mission assurance: ensure public-facing DoD web services have DDoS mitigation and verify leak claims before attributing to compromise. Coordination: share indicators with sector and law-enforcement partners; no sourced basis for further specifics.

provenance.importedSummary: EvilWeb is a pro-Russian hacktivist group created in March 2024 that targets American and European entities using a hack-and-leak method alongside DDoS attacks. The group claims to have obtained data from various high-profile American organizations. EvilWeb announced its participation in the #FreeDurov operation on August 25, 2024, and began executing DDoS and hacking attacks. As of September 3, 2024, their Telegram channel has 1,146 members.
